title: Christian community holds prayer rally in Kolkata against church attacks
seoTitle: Kolkata Christian rally against church attacks

tea.why: Protesters gathered to voice opposition against ongoing mob attacks, vandalism, and threats targeting churches and prayer meetings.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded protection for their community, impartial investigations into the violence, and action against attackers.
tea.changed: Nov 5, 2026: Christian groups held a large prayer rally at Rani Rashmoni Avenue in Kolkata following meetings with RSS leaders.

summary: On November 5, 2026, hundreds of members and leaders from the Christian community gathered for a mega-prayer rally at Rani Rashmoni Avenue in Kolkata's Esplanade area. Organised by the Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP), the demonstration aimed to protest against a wave of mob attacks, vandalism, and intimidation targeting churches, pastors, and prayer gatherings across several districts in West Bengal over a five-month period. Protesters marched from locations such as Sealdah, Birla Planetarium, and Howrah. Organisers reported at least 48 to 65 incidents of violence and harassment, noting that only a fraction resulted in filed FIRs, and rejected allegations of forced conversions. Ahead of the rally, a BCP delegation met with senior Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) functionary Jishnu Basu to raise these concerns, who stated that dialogue would continue while noting concerns regarding conversion allegations.
demands: Stop mob attacks and vandalism against churches and prayer meetings
Investigate violent incidents targeting Christian communities
Take action against failures to register complaints
response: Senior RSS functionary Jishnu Basu stated that dialogue with Christian representatives will continue, while noting that there are genuine concerns about forced conversions that warrant investigation alongside the attacks.

updates.text: Christian organisations and hundreds of participants held a large prayer rally at Rani Rashmoni Avenue in Kolkata.
